goal: Rebuild the landing demo panel so a first-time visitor can actually read and understand one complete example of what Climier does
context: The user looked at this panel and said it feels very cramped and the example is not understandable, and asked for it to be made much better. Measurements from the live page at 1440x900 confirm both halves of that complaint. First, it is cramped: the panel is 1152x385, a 3 to 1 letterbox, and almost every string in it is set below the reading size of the page around it. The counter pills are 10.5px, the lifecycle labels at the bottom are 10.5px, the log rows are 11px, the header command is 11.5 to 12px, the JSON body is 12px, and the explanatory caption is 13px. The satisfied-when table directly below the panel renders at 14px and reads far more easily than the demo that is supposed to sell the product. Second, the example is not understandable, for three separate reasons. (1) The JSON is elided with an ellipsis in the middle of the object in every single phase, so the reader never sees what a command returns; the take phase literally prints id T-auth-0, status in_progress, then the ellipsis, and stops. It is also wrapped with two keys on one line, which is not how the CLI prints it, so it is inaccurate as well as incomplete. (2) The three beats swap on a timer I measured over 30 seconds with zero variance: take holds for 2.9s, submit for 3.8s, accept for 5.1s, looping every 11.7s. Each beat asks the reader to parse an 11 to 16 word caption, a shell command, a JSON body, a log row, four graph nodes and three counters in under 3 to 5 seconds, and then it resets to the beginning, so the story never completes on screen and the log never accumulates. The three captions are the best teaching copy on the page, they explain exactly the non-obvious bits of the model, and the current design gives each of them three seconds and then throws it away. (3) The gate G-auth-prod is drawn nested inside the card of the task it blocks, so blocking reads as containment rather than dependency. On top of all that, at 390x844 the header drops the framing command climier status --initiative auth entirely, leaving counters and a graph with no statement of what produced them, and the 552px right column leaves a 188px pane holding 106px of JSON with the rest empty while the 181px graph is centred in a 289px column. What must not be lost: the three captions word for word, the real CLI commands, the four nodes and their titles, the log rows, the append-only framing, and the dark and light themes. Restructuring and rewriting the component is expected and encouraged, this is a redesign of one component and not a set of tweaks.

targets.intent: Rebuild it as a legible, self-explanatory example that a visitor can read at their own pace. The guiding outcome is that someone arriving on the page mid-cycle can still understand what Climier does and why the graph is honest. Concretely, and in order of importance: the terminal must show a complete and truthfully formatted response with one key per line and no elision anywhere; the progression must stop discarding the story, so the beats accumulate into one continuous example that ends in a complete state before it restarts, with a tempo slow enough to read and a pause control that genuinely holds a beat; and the type must come up to a comfortable reading size, with nothing in the panel below 12px and the caption unmistakably the largest body text in it. Give the panel the room it needs: it may and should grow taller than today, up to roughly 560px at 1440, and its proportions should stop being a letterbox.
targets.notes: Keep the three captions word for word, the commands, the node ids and titles, the log rows and the append-only framing. The existing pause button suggests the panel was always meant to be readable at the reader's pace; make that real rather than decorative. Prefer letting the demo advance and accumulate through take, submit, accept and then restart cleanly, over looping three disconnected snapshots.

targets.selector: figure.landing-panel svg, the graph and its gate card
targets.intent: Make G-auth-prod read as a dependency of T-auth-2 rather than as a card inside it. Task cards and the gate should be visually distinguishable at a glance, the edge treatment should agree with what the satisfied-when table below the panel says about BLOCKS, and the nested box that shares its parent's left edge should go.
targets.notes: The graph has four nodes: T-auth-0 Session contract, T-auth-1 Session store, T-auth-2 Production cutover, and the gate G-auth-prod Cutover approval. It must stay correct in all phases and in both themes.

targets.selector: figure.landing-panel header and footer (the counters row and the lifecycle row)
targets.intent: The counters and the lifecycle stage should read as legible status, not as fine print. The lifecycle row currently reads as a progress bar, with take, submit and accept stretched into three 354px cells joined by hairlines and the active stage marked only by colour; make it read as the lifecycle the captions describe, with the current stage unmistakable. The counter pills and the lifecycle labels must come up to the panel's new type floor. On mobile the framing command climier status --initiative auth must be present, or the panel must state in plain words what it is showing.
targets.notes: The header command, the rev counter and the two icon buttons stay; only their size and hierarchy change.

targets.intent: The three values in each log row, action, actor and node, are spread across the full width with no labels and no grouping, so their meaning has to be guessed. Label them or group them so the row explains itself.
targets.notes: The log is framed as append-only and that framing is part of the lesson; keep it. If the beats accumulate, the log becomes the record of the whole story and should be treated as such.

constraints: Keep the three captions word for word. They are the clearest explanation of the model on the page and this round is about making them readable, not rewriting them.
No text inside the panel below 12px once you are done, and the caption must be the largest body text in the panel.
No ellipsis and no truncated key inside the terminal output in any phase. If the true response does not fit, show a shorter complete response, do not cut one in half.
Use the existing design tokens and the existing component conventions. Do not introduce a new dependency, a new font, or a new colour outside the token set.
Keep it correct in light and dark, and keep the panel inside the page's existing max width.

Keep the change inside the demo panel. If its parent container needs a small adjustment to accommodate the new height, make the smallest one that works and call it out in your response; do not restyle any other landing section. Do not touch the docs chrome, the fonts or the content pages.
Hygiene: run `cd docs && bun run typecheck` and `cd docs && bun run test` and report the exact commands and results in hygiene.
acceptanceCriteria: Scanning computed font-size for every text-bearing element inside figure.landing-panel at 1440x900 reports a minimum of 12px or more, and the caption is the largest body text in the panel.

The terminal output in every phase contains no ellipsis character and no line with two keys on it; each phase shows a complete object and, where the panel is paused, the reader can see the whole response.

The panel tells one accumulating story: over a 60 second observation the log grows or the graph advances across the take, submit and accept beats before anything resets, and no beat is on screen for less than 8 seconds. Verify the timeline with real sampling, not by reading the code.
The pause control holds the current beat: while paused, sampling the panel every 200ms for 5 seconds shows no change of command and no change of caption.
At 390x844 the framing command or an equivalent plain-words statement of what the panel shows is visible in the header.
The gate G-auth-prod is no longer drawn inside the card of T-auth-2, and the three graph states in the three beats remain correct.
The panel at 1440x900 is taller than 385px, is no wider than about 2.6 to 1, and contains no pane with a large empty run inside it.
`cd docs && bun run typecheck` exits 0, `cd docs && bun run test` passes, and `cd docs && bun run build` succeeds.
qualityChecks: Read one full cycle as a first-time visitor: is the example understandable without prior knowledge of Climier? If any step needs the reader to infer what a value means, fix it.
The panel should be as easy to read as the satisfied-when table directly below it. Use that table as the local benchmark for type size and breathing room.
Do not solve the height problem by adding empty padding. If a pane is empty, it is either doing work or it should not be there.
The three captions should feel like the spine of the panel, not a footer note.
Check that the new tempo feels deliberate rather than slow, and that the reset, when it comes, is clean and obviously a restart.
Verify dark mode as carefully as light mode, especially the accent on the newly ready node and the log separator.
regressionChecks: The landing page as a whole at 1440: the hero, the buttons, the panel, the section below it and the footer. A taller panel must not break the rhythm or push the next section awkwardly.
Landing at 1024, 768 and 390 in light and dark.
A full cycle of all three beats in light and dark, checking the graph, the counters, the terminal, the log and the lifecycle row in each.
The rest of the landing must be untouched: the dot field, the band, the satisfied-when table, the code blocks and the footer.
Scrolling the page past the panel and back, to confirm nothing is left mid-transition and the off-screen animation gating still holds.

visualGaps.expected: Readable at the reader's own pace, accumulating instead of resetting, with a pause control that holds.
